story.title: Designing Around Limestone and Tide: Quriyat's Careful New Chapter for Hawiyat Najm
story.seo_title: Hawiyat Najm Park Adds Cycling & Eco-Camping in Quriyat
story.meta_description: Muscat Municipality upgrades Hawiyat Najm (Bimmah Sinkhole) Park in Quriyat with cycling tracks, serviced camping, solar power, and native flora.

detail.extracted_title: Designing Around Limestone and Tide: Quriyat's Careful New Chapter for Hawiyat Najm
detail.excerpt: At Oman's famous sea-fed coastal sinkhole, Muscat Municipality is adding cycling trails, serviced camping, and solar-powered amenities without disturbing the rock rim or its older trees.
detail.article_html:
Anyone who has driven south along the coast of Wilayat Quriyat knows the quiet surprise of Hawiyat Najm—known internationally as Bimmah Sinkhole. Across an open, sun-bleached limestone plateau between the Eastern Hajar foothills and the Gulf of Oman, the ground suddenly drops away into a wide circular cavern where underground channels feed clear, turquoise seawater in and out with the tide.

For years, most visitors treated the site as a brief roadside stop: walk to the stone parapet, descend the stairs to dip a hand into the cool brackish pool, take a photograph, and return to the highway. Now, Muscat Municipality is carrying out a comprehensive redevelopment of Hawiyat Najm Park aimed at turning that quick pause into an unhurried full-day or overnight stay—while keeping the geological formation and its existing trees untouched at the center of the plan.

Trails, Cycling Loops, and Overnight Camping

Rather than crowding the edge of the sinkhole itself, the new master plan spreads visitor activity gently across the surrounding parkland. Dedicated pedestrian walkways and cycling tracks loop through the site so walkers and cyclists can take in the coastal plateau and mountain views at their own pace.

For visitors who want to stay past sunset, the project introduces designated camping zones equipped with essential utilities and service facilities, balancing outdoor immersion with comfort and family privacy. Elsewhere across the grounds, Muscat Municipality is adding multi-purpose sports courts, a shaded children's playground, cafés, landscaped gardens, and quiet seating corners designed to blend into the terrain rather than compete with it.

Solar Lighting and Native Flora First

Developing a fragile karst limestone landmark comes with obvious ecological risks, from light pollution and water waste to root damage around older trees. According to project details, preserving the site's existing mature trees and natural rock features sits at the core of the engineering brief.

New landscaping relies on drought-hardy plants adapted to Quriyat's warm coastal climate, watered through efficient, low-consumption irrigation networks. Select park buildings and pathway lighting systems run on solar power paired with energy-saving fixtures, keeping the park's operational footprint light after dusk.

A Stronger Anchor on Quriyat's Coast

Speaking on the project's design, Eng. Muzna bint Ahmed Al Salmani noted that bringing eco-tourism, outdoor sports, family leisure, and serviced camping together inside one site gives visitors practical reasons to spend an entire day—or weekend—in Wilayat Quriyat.

Aligned with Oman Vision 2040 goals for sustainable regional tourism and everyday quality of life, the upgraded park positions Quriyat as an active coastal destination in its own right, proving that thoughtfully planned public infrastructure can widen access to a natural wonder while leaving its ancient limestone rim intact.

  • Oman Daily
detail.instagram_caption:
Set into a coastal limestone plateau in Wilayat Quriyat, Hawiyat Najm—known around the world as Bimmah Sinkhole—has long been one of Oman's most striking geological formations, fed underground by clear turquoise seawater. Now, Muscat Municipality is redeveloping Hawiyat Najm Park to turn a quick roadside stop into a thoughtful full-day and overnight outdoor destination.

The upgrade introduces dedicated pedestrian walkways, cycling paths, sports courts, family play zones, cafés, and serviced camping areas designed for comfort and privacy—while preserving every existing mature tree and rock formation, running select facilities on solar power, and watering climate-adapted native plants through low-consumption irrigation.

Read the full story at omanspire.om (link in bio).
